analysis:
Reviewed unit 0 and all supplied integration replay, including three native-runtime gitlink replacements at libs/mlx:1, libs/mlx-swift:1 and libs/mlx-swift-lm:1, plus docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md:859–974. No independently supported security regression is visible. The documentation retains fail-closed checkpoint identity (912–913), text-only reuse (920–921), backend capability gates (922–924), and reservation release on cancellation, refusal and unload (925–927). These are documented contracts, not implementation verification. Historical test evidence at 864–881 does not qualify the newly combined dependency revisions.
The prior analysis describes a new demanded-latest-checkpoint policy at docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md:670–689, but that source and its BASE comparison are omitted from this replay; its preservation of donation gates cannot be independently confirmed here. The replay is explicitly incomplete, and the gitlinks provide no internal dependency diffs. Missing implementation is a material coverage limit, not proof of a vulnerability or safety.
Further review should inspect the three pinned dependency diffs and the associated provider activation of demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens: dense-Qwen/paged eligibility, aligned checkpoint bounds, donation demand, scheduler/projection agreement, ownership, and cancellation/rollback cleanup. Validate interactions with T-041's authenticated cacheSalt, verified runtime identity, HMAC disk naming, encrypted payloads, TTL and write/staging budgets. Native execution also implicates TB-007, A-001, T-007, T-010 and T-028. Broader checkpoint coverage may change cache exposure and availability, but the supplied evidence does not establish weakened isolation, crypto, authorization or billing controls. Remaining uncertainty is material to these dependency changes and requires implementation review.
